content_preview.summary: Kiro's 2.36.0 changelog adds Approve for me to interactive V3 sessions; its docs say it judges only actions no rule settles and does not replace security controls.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Kiro CLI 2.36.0, dated October 29, 2026 in the [Kiro changelog](https://kiro.dev/changelog/cli/2-36/), adds a feature called "Approve for me" to interactive V3 sessions. The changelog says "Kiro approves routine actions for you, blocks risky ones, and asks when unsure." Release 2.37.0 followed on [October 30, 2026](https://kiro.dev/changelog/cli/2-37/).

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear 682-word Briefing with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. Stays attributive throughout ('The changelog says', 'The documentation states'). Minor nit: the section 'Other Approval Changes in 2.36.0 and 2.37.0' also lists automatic V2 agent upgrades, which is not strictly an approval change. Title is about 120 characters (under 150).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three gzipped snapshots (source-0, source-1, source-2 .html.gz; HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all). Pages are Next.js; changelog bullet text was extracted from the embedded flight payload and the docs page from rendered text. First-party only: all three sources are Kiro's own changelog and documentation pages on kiro.dev (allowlisted; no new host added). The writer found no independent coverage and the article discloses this in 'What We Don't Know'; this is a Briefing, so the Analysis independence requirement does not apply. source-0 (2.36.0 changelog, dated October 29, 2026, version 2.36.0): confirms 'Kiro approves routine actions for you, blocks risky ones, and asks when unsure', deny/ask/allow decide first, 'Approved for you' marking, /permissions > Policies, approve-for-me preset stored per workspace, 'Kiro keeps asking' when unavailable, the git stash pop rule-picker bullet (with 'git stash *' and 'git *' links), kiro-cli agent upgrade warnings, and the V2 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL ask-first bullet. source-1 (2.37.0 changelog, dated October 30, 2026): confirms automatic V2 agent upgrades on by default at V3 start, in-place rewrite with .json.bak backup, 'kiro-cli settings chat.enableAutoAgentUpgrade false' keeps agents in V2, and V3 approval prompts show only the first line with Ctrl+O to see the rest. (The page also lists a 2.37.1 patch dated Oct 31, 2026, which the article does not mention; not an error.) source-2 (permissions docs): confirms 'deny > ask > allow > evaluate', the evaluate effect, preset allows workspace reads/writes and read-only shell commands, verbatim 'Approve for me currently uses Claude Sonnet 4.6 to judge each unsettled action.', 'Approve for me can still block an action or ask you' (contrast with --trust-all-tools and /tools trust-all), verbatim 'Approve for me does not replace your security controls', deny-rule and local-sandbox recommendation, 'A file operation outside the workspace is not judged by Approve for me and keeps its ordinary prompt', 'Kiro also asks whenever it is unsure, and whenever the trust classifier is unavailable', /permissions not available in cloud sessions, and the three tiers (exact, subcommand 'git stash *', pattern 'git *') with no pattern tiers for sudo/env-prefixed commands. Version and date attribution between 2.36.0 (Oct 29) and 2.37.0 (Oct 30) is correct for every bullet. Every quote checked verbatim against the snapshots.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, version, date, quote, command and setting name traced to a snapshot; no discrepancies found. The Claude Sonnet 4.6 mention is a verbatim quote from the docs and is presented as Kiro's statement ('currently'). Both internal Herald links resolve to published articles.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive. Kiro's security statement is reported as the documentation's own language and its recommendations, with no endorsement or evaluation of effectiveness; 'What We Don't Know' states that criteria, approval rates and adversarial performance are not documented.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior Herald article covers Kiro CLI or Approve for me (only the Kiro Crew article from 2026-08). The Context section links the Copilot assisted-permissions (2026-10/27) and Claude Code auto mode (2026-10/01) articles without comparing them.
concerns: All sources are first-party (Kiro changelog and docs); no independent verification of how the feature behaves, which the article discloses.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed Briefing; all claims verified against the snapshots. Approve. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate coverage of a notable but single-vendor permission-mode feature for a defined developer audience
